edit.description: `fold_file_id` (384) folds every directory between `base` and the file into the id, so a `notes/*.md` template's `notes/home.md` is keyed `notes-home` — a key no author declared, and the one `splice_name` would place back at `notes/notes-home.md`. Identity is a declared fact (file stem or starred segment), and a literal template segment is locus, never identity: folding earns its keep only for the directories a wildcard spans, where depth genuinely distinguishes same-named files (the `**/CLAUDE.md` nearest-wins nesting its own doc comment names). The fold strips what its pattern spells literally, leaving `**`-spanned placement folded exactly as today; uniqueness is unaffected, since every member under one pattern shares that literal prefix. The header's `import::wholefile_id` cite resolves to nothing at HEAD and rides this edit.

`read_file_unit`'s nested-file caller (956) hands `found.host_unit` as the fold base while the host template's pattern is the host kind's own declared fact, so the literal prefix is derivable at exactly the site that folds; the `governs`-scanned branch just below passes the kind's root against its own glob — the same (locus, pattern) pair, one rule for both. Whichever half holds the strip, both callers reach it.

`splice_name` (988) is the inverse the fold has to agree with — it re-inserts the literal segments verbatim and splices the name into the final one. If the literal-prefix derivation belongs beside the one splice rule rather than inside the fold, it lands here; the splice's own behaviour is unchanged either way.

`NESTED_FILE_SUBDIRECTORY_PROGRAM` (264) emits `notes/checklist.md` and is never read back, so the disagreement is unpinned: the lane gains the check-side half — the discovered child's key is `checklist` and its address `guide:operate-the-gate/supporting-doc/checklist`, never `…/notes-checklist`.

`NestedFileUnit` (193) is where the host template's `pattern` is in hand — `discover_nested_file` scans the locus with it (255) — while the fold's one production caller holds only `found.host_unit` as its base, so if the literal prefix travels on the unit rather than being re-derived at the fold, it lands here. `unit_dir` (245) is unchanged either way.

The `subdir-CLAUDE` memory fold (2001) is the `**`-spanned case the strip must leave exactly as it is — `**/CLAUDE.md` spells no literal directory, so the ids stand; verify rather than assume, which is what the acceptance names.

summary: A nested child's key is its file stem, not its placement: the fold strips the directories its template already spells literally, so fold and splice are inverses

tests.asserts: a child under a `notes/*.md` template is discovered under the key its author declared, and a `**`-spanned fold still distinguishes same-named files at different depths

acceptance: `cargo test` green, with the `notes/*.md` fixture's emitted child read back under the authored key and `tests/it/read_verbs.rs`'s `subdir-CLAUDE` memory fold untouched.
notes: Routed from inbox note 2 (observed at b038eec9; the forward window touches specs/ only). Re-verified at HEAD: the fold and the splice are both as reported, but `refuse_ungoverned` does **not** fire — `notes/notes-home.md` still matches `notes/*.md` — so the verified gap is identity, not the glob round trip: the key a discovery reads is not the name its author declared. Independent of depth, hence its own entry. scoped at 640cb4fd
